title: Capacity reshuffle: deferred hires vs. credit line analysis
body:
Purpose:
This working worksheet evaluates a hybrid operational response to an emergent token-demand surge: delaying a tranche of hires (deferred FTEs) vs. drawing a short-term credit line to cover burst capacity and contractor labor. Goal: identify the lowest expected P&L impact and preserve SLA-critical feature delivery while keeping runway risk within tolerance.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Recommendation: adopt a 60/40 plan (60% credit-line-backed short-term capacity + contractors; 40% deferred-hire phasing over 12 weeks) with strict triggers.
- Why: preserves near-term throughput for enterprise customers (keeps Dedicated commitments intact), reduces permanent hiring commitments if demand normalizes, and caps marginal cost exposure via priced credit.
- Expected P&L delta (6 months): incremental net cash outflow range $1.1M–$1.8M depending on token-price and spot-GPU movements. NPV of deferred hires (12 months) is ~+$0.6M vs. immediate hires if demand falls back.

Context and constraints:
- Current state: 3 consecutive weeks of +18% M/M token demand; utilization forecasts show sustained +10–12% baseline uplift over next 3 months in optimistic, +25% in stress scenario.
- Runway target: maintain >14 months of runway under base case.
- SLA exposure: two enterprise customers are within 5% of committed p99 latency targets; loss of Dedicated throughput results in SLA credits that could exceed $300k monthly if capacity not preserved.

Options considered (brief):
A) Immediate hiring (baseline) — convert all open requisitions to FTE starts within 45 days.
B) Deferred hires — freeze 50–75% of open reqs and phase over 12–24 weeks.
C) Short-term credit line + contractors — $2.5M 90-day facility to fund contractors and cloud GPU spot burst.
D) Hybrid (recommended) — mix of B & C with automated triggers.

Assumptions used in calculations (conservative unless noted):
- Fully loaded annual cost per new FTE: engineering (infra/serving/runtime) $220k; applied ML $200k; SRE $200k.
- Contractor blended rate (equivalent output): $140/hr fully loaded (assume 80 hrs/week per FTE equivalent conversion factor of 0.65 throughput).
- GPU spot burst marginal cost: $4.2k per node-week average (varies by region); reserved per-month equivalent $14k/node.
- Interest / facility fee for credit line: 6% APR + 1% origination fee for 90-day facility (effective cost ~1.7% for 90 days on capital used).
- SLA credit exposure if capacity shortfall >10%: $300k/mo incremental.
- Probability multipliers: base-case demand sustainment (45%), reversion to mean (30%), stress sustained (25%).

Numeric sensitivity snapshot (6-month horizon):
Scenario 1 — Reversion to mean (30%):
- Action: defer 70% of hires, draw 35% of proposed credit (~$875k).
- Incremental cash outflow: contractors + spot = $420k; credit facility cost ~ $15k (90d) + origination; SLA risk minimal.
- Net: ~ $435k incremental cost vs immediate hire.

Scenario 2 — Sustained uplift (45%):
- Action: hybrid 60/40 credit/hire. Draw $1.5M facility, start top-priority 40% FTEs (phased).
- Incremental cash outflow: contractors + spot = $780k; facility cost (90d & interest) ~$30k; new FTE ramp costs (first 6 months pro-rated) ~$880k.
- SLA mitigation avoids $900k of potential credits (estimate).
- Net: +$770k incremental cash outflow but prevents potential $900k+ SLA losses — favorable to avoid churn.

Scenario 3 — Stress sustained (25%):
- Action: accelerate hires to full and increase facility to $2.5M, convert contractors to temp-to-perm where possible.
- Incremental cash outflow: ~$1.8M (6 months), facility cost ~ $45k; but prevents repeated SLA credits and potential churn losses >$2.4M.

Headcount phasing table (example plan for 12-week hybrid):
Week windows: W0-4, W5-8, W9-12
- Priority group A (must hire): 4 infra eng (ramp 1 each window), 2 SRE (both W0-4)
- Priority group B (conditional): 3 applied ML (W5-12), 2 infra (W9-12)
- Deferred pool: remaining 6 open reqs (freeze until trigger)
Estimated 6-month P&L effect (base/hybrid):
- Immediate-hire baseline (all onboarded): incremental payroll run-rate add ~$2.8M (6 months pro-rated).
- Hybrid (60/40): payroll add ~$1.1M + contractor/spot costs ~$0.78M + facility costs $0.03M = ~$1.91M (6 months).
- Deferred-heavy (70% deferred): payroll add ~$0.6M + contractor/spot $0.42M = ~$1.02M (6 months).

Pricing sensitivity matrix (impact on margin and hire decision):
- Token price increase +20% (market-level pass-through unlikely): gross margin compression vs. token-weighted revenue = -3.6 percentage points over 6 months under current mix. This increases need to preserve throughput for high-margin enterprise routes.
- GPU spot price +30%: increases burst cost linearly; facility draw increases by ~+$120k over 6 months in worst-case.
- Customer churn risk: each 1% increase in p99 latency breach correlates with ~0.8% revenue churn over 3 months in prior cohort analysis.

Decision triggers (proposed automated gates):
1) Utilization trigger: sustained rolling-3wk token demand > +15% -> move to hybrid (draw initial 50% facility tranche).
2) SLA trigger: rise in p99 errors or >5% of premium routes suffering latency breach -> immediate contractor scaling and second tranche draw.
3) Runway trigger: if credit utilization + committed payroll > 42% of remaining runway-adjusted free cash -> pause hires and reassess.
4) Reversion trigger: if rolling-4wk demand drops below +5% -> halt facility draws and accelerate hire deferrals to avoid overpayment of contractors.

Operational runbook (short):
- Week 0: finance issues term sheet w/ credit provider; legal approves facility docs; talent ops issues contractor offer templates; hiring managers reconfirm priority list.
- Week 1–4: deploy contractors on highest-impact infra tickets, launch spot-burst capacity in targeted regions, monitor SLA delta daily.
- Week 4: review demand curves vs triggers; decide on second tranche or throttling.
- Week 8–12: begin measured onboarding of priority FTEs per phasing plan if triggers still active.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: credit facility draw creates debt covenant pressure if demand collapses. Mitigation: 90-day facility, rollback clause, pre-specified re-pricing if utilization <20% after 60 days.
- Risk: contractors deliver lower throughput than FTE equivalents. Mitigation: use proven vendor partners, attach acceptance metrics to SOWs, and limit contractor tenure to 12 weeks before conversion review.
- Risk: optics to market / investors. Mitigation: narrative that facility is prudent short-term liquidity tool vs. permanent hiring.

Open questions for leadership (notes to CFO/GC/Head of Talent):
- Appetite for up to $2.5M facility with 1.0% origination vs. ability to use internal committed credit?
- What portion of SLA exposure are we comfortable assuming vs. paying contractors?
- Candidate pipeline health — can we guarantee time-to-productivity if we accelerate hiring? (talent ops input required)

Recommended next steps (for this doc iteration):
1) Run a 10k Monte Carlo (finance) on token demand, GPU spot prices, and SLA events to produce a probabilistic P&L overlay.
2) Legal to draft a 90-day facility term sheet with rollback clauses and a max utilization covenant.
3) Talent ops to produce a 12-week contractor SOW and a prioritized requisition list aligned to the phasing table.
4) Product & SRE to produce a short evaluation of feature-level SLA sensitivity (which routes to throttle if needed).

Appendix (quick reference numbers):
- Example fully loaded FTE (eng): $220k/yr -> $110k over 6 months (pro rata).
- Contractor equivalent: $140/hr -> ~$115k for 6 months at 40 hrs/week (but 0.65 throughput effective).
- Facility economics: $1M drawn for 90 days @ 6% APR = interest ~$15k + origination 1% = $10k.

Notes / drafting history:
- Drafted by Avery Chen (Finance) 2026-05-12.
- Inputs: token-demand-forecast sheet, infra-capacity model (SRE), legal credit checklist.
- Next edit planned after Monte Carlo outputs (target 2026-06-07).

This is a working doc; please add comments inline or append a short note in the linked GoogleSheet when you change an assumption.
